BUS.G11.T1.ACQUIRE.A1.title: Avenues of acquiring a business
BUS.G11.T1.ACQUIRE.A1.description: Ways of acquiring a business — franchising, outsourcing and leasing — with their advantages, disadvantages and contractual implications such as royalties and legalities.
BUS.G11.T1.ACQUIRE.A1.strand: T1 — Business environments, socio-economic issues, sectors, ownership & acquiring a business
BUS.G11.T1.ACQUIRE.A1.recovery_strategy: Franchising = buy the right to trade under a proven brand and pay royalties. Outsourcing = pay another firm to do a task for you. Leasing = rent an asset instead of buying it.

questions.question: Buying the right to trade under an established brand, using its name and system, is called _________.
options: franchising
outsourcing
leasing
auditing
questions.memo: Franchising means buying the right to run a business under a proven brand's name and system, usually in return for fees and royalties.

questions.question: Paying another company to handle a task or function for you, such as cleaning or payroll, is called _________.
options: outsourcing
franchising
leasing
lobbying
questions.memo: Outsourcing is paying an outside firm to perform a task instead of doing it in-house.

questions.question: Renting an asset such as equipment or premises instead of buying it is called _________.
options: leasing
franchising
outsourcing
merging
questions.memo: Leasing is paying to use an asset for a period without owning it — for example renting machines or a shop.

questions.question: True or false: A franchisee usually pays the franchisor royalties.
options: True
False
questions.memo: A franchisee typically pays ongoing royalties (and often an initial fee) to the franchisor for the right to use the brand and system.

questions.question: In franchising, the person who buys the right to run the branded business is called the _________.
options: franchisee
franchisor
lessor
auditor
questions.memo: The franchisor owns the brand and sells the rights; the franchisee buys those rights and runs the outlet.

questions.question: True or false: When you lease an asset, you become its legal owner immediately.
options: True
False
questions.memo: Leasing gives you the use of an asset but not ownership — the lessor still owns it.

questions.question: Sort each example under the avenue of acquiring a business it illustrates.

items.text: Opening a branch of a national fast-food brand and paying royalties
Hiring an outside firm to run the company's payroll
Renting delivery vehicles instead of buying them
Running a branded coffee shop under licence from the brand owner
Paying a security company to guard the premises
Renting the shop premises from a landlord

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Trading under a brand for royalties is franchising; paying an outside firm to do a task is outsourcing; renting assets is leasing.

questions.question: What is an advantage of buying a franchise rather than starting a business from scratch?
options: You trade under a proven brand with an established system and support
You never have to pay any fees
You can ignore the franchisor's rules
You automatically owe no tax
questions.expected: You trade under a proven brand with an established system and support
questions.memo: A franchise comes with a known brand, a tested business model and franchisor support, which lowers the risk of starting alone.

questions.question: What is a disadvantage of franchising for the franchisee?
options: You must pay royalties and follow the franchisor's rules, limiting your freedom
You get no brand recognition at all
You can never make a profit
You are forced to invent your own product
questions.expected: You must pay royalties and follow the franchisor's rules, limiting your freedom
questions.memo: Franchisees pay ongoing royalties and must stick to the franchisor's system, so they have less independence than an owner starting fresh.

questions.question: An advantage of outsourcing a task such as IT support is that the business can _________.
options: focus on what it does best while experts handle the task
stop paying any staff ever again
avoid all contracts
ignore the quality of the work
questions.expected: focus on what it does best while experts handle the task
questions.memo: Outsourcing lets a business concentrate on its core work and hand specialist tasks to firms that do them well, often at lower cost.

questions.question: True or false: Leasing equipment instead of buying it helps a new business preserve its cash.
options: True
False
questions.memo: Leasing spreads the cost over time rather than requiring a large upfront purchase, which helps a new business keep cash for other needs.

questions.question: Thesis: 'A first-time owner should buy a franchise rather than start a brand-new business.' Choose the THREE strongest supporting reasons.
questions.thesis: A first-time owner should buy a franchise rather than start a brand-new business.

pool.text: The brand is already known, so customers come more easily
The franchisor provides a proven system and training
There is a lower risk of failure than starting from nothing
A franchisee never has to pay any royalties
The franchise sign is a nice colour
A franchise lets you ignore the franchisor's rules

questions.memo: The strong reasons are brand recognition, a proven system with training, and lower risk. The others are false (royalties are paid, rules must be followed) or irrelevant.

questions.question: A business pays a specialist firm to manage its cleaning so its own staff can focus on production. This is an example of:
options: outsourcing
franchising
leasing
a merger
questions.memo: Handing a non-core task (cleaning) to an outside firm is outsourcing.

questions.question: Sort each item into whether it is an advantage or a disadvantage of franchising for the franchisee.

items.text: Ongoing royalty payments to the franchisor
Training and support from the franchisor
Strict rules that limit the owner's freedom

questions.expected: All six items in correct buckets (or ≥75%)
questions.memo: Advantages: brand recognition, support, a proven model. Disadvantages: royalties, strict rules and a high initial fee.

questions.question: What is a contractual implication a franchisee must accept?
options: A legal agreement to pay royalties and follow the franchisor's standards
Complete freedom to change the brand's products
No obligations of any kind
Ownership of the franchisor's entire brand
questions.expected: A legal agreement to pay royalties and follow the franchisor's standards
questions.memo: The franchise contract legally binds the franchisee to pay royalties and uphold the franchisor's standards and rules.

questions.question: A start-up rents its machinery rather than buying it outright. Which avenue of acquiring resources is this, and why might it suit a start-up?
options: Leasing — it avoids a large upfront cost and preserves cash
Franchising — it gives the start-up a famous brand
Outsourcing — it hands production to another firm
A merger — it combines two businesses
questions.expected: Leasing — it avoids a large upfront cost and preserves cash
questions.memo: Renting machinery is leasing, which spreads cost and keeps cash free — useful for a start-up with limited capital.

questions.question: A franchisee wants to sell a completely new product the franchisor does not allow. What does the franchise agreement most likely mean for this plan?
options: The franchisee is bound by the contract to follow the franchisor's product range
The franchisee can ignore the contract freely
The contract has no effect on products
The franchisee automatically owns the brand
questions.expected: The franchisee is bound by the contract to follow the franchisor's product range
questions.memo: Franchise contracts require franchisees to stick to the approved system and product range, so the franchisee cannot simply add an unapproved product.

questions.question: A business is deciding between outsourcing its deliveries and buying its own fleet. Which best evaluates outsourcing here?
options: It avoids the cost and management of a fleet but means relying on another firm's reliability
It is always cheaper and carries no risks at all
It forces the business to buy vehicles anyway
It has no effect on cost or control
questions.expected: It avoids the cost and management of a fleet but means relying on another firm's reliability
questions.memo: Outsourcing deliveries saves the cost and effort of owning a fleet, but the business becomes dependent on the outside firm's reliability and quality.

questions.question: Why might an established franchisor benefit from selling franchises rather than opening all the outlets itself?
options: It expands faster using franchisees' capital and effort while earning fees and royalties
It gives away its brand for free
It loses all income from the outlets
It must run every outlet personally
questions.expected: It expands faster using franchisees' capital and effort while earning fees and royalties
questions.memo: Franchising lets the franchisor grow quickly using franchisees' money and management, while collecting fees and royalties — a benefit to both sides.

questions.question: Which situation best calls for outsourcing rather than franchising or leasing?
options: A firm wants a specialist to handle its accounting so it can focus on its core work
A person wants to run a branded outlet of a national chain
A business wants to use machines without buying them
A business wants to combine fully with a competitor
questions.expected: A firm wants a specialist to handle its accounting so it can focus on its core work
questions.memo: Handing a specialist task like accounting to an outside expert is outsourcing. The other situations describe franchising, leasing and a merger.
